key_concepts: Friction is a force that opposes motion
Friction acts in the opposite direction to an object's movement
Friction causes moving objects to slow down and eventually stop
Static friction prevents an object at rest from moving against a surface
Static friction is present between surfaces that are in contact
A greater applied force can overcome static friction and start motion
Heavier objects experience stronger static friction than lighter objects
Kinetic friction acts opposite the motion of a moving object
Kinetic friction depends on the nature of the surfaces in contact
Rough surfaces produce more friction while smooth surfaces produce less friction
Kinetic friction includes rolling, sliding, and fluid friction
When static friction is overcome, an object moves with kinetic friction
